name: C2CAD-Bench
description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating language-agnostic 3D spatial reasoning in large language models. The dataset contains natural-language CAD-style prompts, deterministic golden JSON references, model JSON outputs, and per-case scores for 25 test families, 75 test cases, and 13 evaluated LLMs.
rai:dataCollection: All benchmark cases are synthetic CAD-style tasks authored and generated by the benchmark authors through family-specific Python generators in stages/. Released model outputs were collected by querying model APIs with the released prompts, extracting JSON-array outputs, and scoring them against deterministic golden references.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A single human reviewer manually verified the procedurally generated benchmark cases and deterministic golden JSON references for correctness, geometric consistency, and family-specific constraints before release. Ground-truth geometry itself is produced by deterministic family generators rather than by a human annotation workforce.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts, golden references, and model outputs are packaged into JSONL and CSV artifacts for release.
Model outputs are normalized into a canonical primitive schema before deterministic coverage, geometry, semantic, and global scoring.

rai:dataLimitations: C2CAD-Bench measures coordinate-level primitive assembly reasoning in a restricted vocabulary of seven primitives. It does not evaluate full CAD workflows, constraint solvers, manufacturability, physical simulation, tolerancing, or downstream design usability.

The released v1.0 prompts are the exact evaluated prompts and include varying levels of scaffolding, including explicit counts, vectors, axis anchors, and some formula-like hints. Scores should therefore not be interpreted as a pure zero-scaffolding measure of spatial reasoning.
The benchmark is a fixed synthetic snapshot of 75 cases across 25 families, so coverage of real-world engineering domains, materials, and organization-specific CAD conventions is limited.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark over-represents tasks that can be expressed as deterministic primitive assemblies and may favor models that are strong at structured coordinate generation and JSON formatting over models better suited to higher-level design exploration.

Family selection and scoring emphasize symmetry, regularity, connectivity, clearances, and bio-inspired procedural patterns chosen by the benchmark authors. This can bias rankings toward those design motifs and away from open-ended or stylistic CAD tasks.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None expected. The released dataset contains synthetic CAD-style prompts, deterministic golden references, model-generated JSON outputs, and aggregate scores; it is not built from human-subject records, personal profiles, medical data, or scraped user content.
rai:dataUseCases: Recommended uses: benchmarking and diagnosing LLM performance on coordinate-level 3D spatial reasoning, structured JSON primitive assembly generation, ablation studies on prompting and parsing, and reproducible evaluation of CAD-oriented reasoning systems.

Not established for: certifying real-world CAD competency, manufacturability, safety-critical engineering design, physical simulation fidelity, or production deployment without additional CAD-kernel checks and human-expert review.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impact: the benchmark can improve transparent and reproducible evaluation of spatial reasoning systems and expose failure modes before deployment in engineering-assistive workflows. Negative impact and misuse risk: leaderboard optimization may encourage overfitting to released prompts, and benchmark success may be overstated as evidence of broader engineering competence. The dataset should therefore be used as a diagnostic benchmark, not as a safety or professional qualification signal.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Synthetic benchmark generation
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: The dataset was created de novo by the authors using deterministic Python generators that produce synthetic CAD-style prompts and golden JSON primitive assemblies across 25 benchmark families and 3 difficulty levels. No external parent dataset was used.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Model output collection
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Released model outputs were collected by querying commercial and hosted LLM APIs with the benchmark prompts, extracting JSON-array outputs, and storing the normalized responses and scores as part of the benchmark artifact.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Synthetic case validation and exclusion
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Procedurally generated benchmark cases were reviewed for schema validity, geometric consistency, and family-specific rule satisfaction. Cases or outputs that failed deterministic validation, contained malformed geometry, or violated benchmark construction constraints were corrected or excluded before the release snapshot was finalized.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Human verification of synthetic benchmark cases
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: A single human reviewer manually verified the procedurally generated benchmark cases and their deterministic golden JSON references for correctness, geometric consistency, and family-specific constraints before release. The benchmark content was generated synthetically; the human role was verification and quality control rather than primary manual data annotation.
